scenes.heading: Building a customer retention flow instead of only chasing new sales

sents.d: Building a customer retention flow instead of only chasing new sales
Repeat customers are usually more profitable than constantly acquiring new ones.
Acquiring a new customer is typically more expensive than keeping an existing one, yet many new stores focus entirely on acquisition and never build a retention system.
A basic post-purchase email flow — delivery updates, a review request, and a follow-up offer — captures value that would otherwise be left on the table.
Segmenting past customers for repeat-purchase promotions or early access to new products often produces a better return than the same budget spent on new cold traffic.
Tracking repeat purchase rate alongside new customer count gives a clearer picture of whether the business is actually building momentum or just replacing churned customers every month.

take: Build a retention flow, not just a stream of new buyers.
